title: A gap report

blocks.text: A planning team's dashboard shows every solve's gap, and finance asked why HiGHS and SCIP runs of the same scenario report slightly different percentages. Write `gap_report(primal, dual)` in `gaps.py`. `primal` is the incumbent's objective value (infinite, with either sign, when no plan was found) and `dual` is the best bound. It returns a dict with three entries:

items: `"absolute"`: the distance between the two numbers, never negative;
`"relative_highs"`: the absolute gap divided by the size of the incumbent;
`"relative_scip"`: the absolute gap divided by the smaller of the two numbers in size.

blocks.text: When there is no plan, every entry is `None`. A relative gap whose divisor is zero is `None` too: a dashboard must not show a made-up number. When there is a plan but no bound has been proved yet (`dual` infinite, with either sign), the gap is not unknown but unbounded: the absolute gap is `math.inf`, and so is each relative gap whose divisor is not zero. The function works for maximizations and minimizations alike. About ten lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
import math

from gaps import gap_report


def rounded(report):
    return {k: None if v is None else round(v, 4) for k, v in report.items()}


print("plan 450, bound 500:", rounded(gap_report(450.0, 500.0)))
print("plan 1200, bound 1150:", rounded(gap_report(1200.0, 1150.0)))
print("plan -30, bound -25:", rounded(gap_report(-30.0, -25.0)))
print("plan 0, bound 12:", rounded(gap_report(0.0, 12.0)))
print("no plan, bound 800:", rounded(gap_report(math.inf, 800.0)))

cases.says: a maximization's gaps divide the absolute gap by the incumbent
the absolute gap is positive whichever side the bound is on
SCIP's convention divides by the smaller of the two numbers in size
with no plan every entry of the report is None
an incumbent of zero gives no relative gap, never a huge number
a plan with no proven bound has an infinite gap, never None
